## Paper

Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms

## World

cross_world_methods

## Institution

Not applicable: method paper.

## Agent type

On-policy actor-critic / PPO.

## Theoretical benchmark

No economic-theory benchmark. The method benchmark is empirical comparison against other online policy-gradient methods on standard RL tasks.

## Learning setup

PPO alternates on-policy rollout collection with minibatch epochs over a clipped surrogate objective, value-function learning, advantage estimates, and entropy regularization.

## Metrics

Paper-side: average episodic return, learning curves, sample complexity, simplicity, and wall-time. Repo-side: world metrics and finite-run validation outputs.

## Main result

PPO outperforms other online policy gradient methods and strikes a favorable balance between sample complexity, simplicity, and wall-time.

## What they prove

The paper motivates the clipped surrogate objective as a practical first-order policy-gradient method. Treat PPO here as an implementation and empirical benchmark obligation, not as a formal guarantee of monotonic improvement in this repo's economic worlds.

## What they only simulate

Empirical performance on benchmark control/game tasks, including robotic locomotion and Atari-style settings.

## What they do NOT test

Institutional economic worlds, collusion/exploitability metrics, auction/matching benchmarks, and the cross-world capability ladder used in this repo.

## What we need to reproduce

Do not reproduce Atari/MuJoCo for this thesis. Reproduce the method-level obligation: categorical discrete policy, clipped surrogate updates, old log probabilities, advantage estimation, value loss, entropy bonus, and repeated minibatch epochs, then compare PPO against Q-learning/DQN/MARL inside the artificial-economies worlds.

## How our project differs

The paper validates PPO as a general RL algorithm on standard control/game benchmarks. This repo adapts PPO to structured observations and discrete economic actions, then asks whether its learned economic behavior differs from tabular Q-learning, DQN, independent-DQN, and centralized-critic agents.

## Implementation obligations

Categorical discrete policy; separate value function; stored old log probabilities; GAE-style advantage computation; clipped surrogate probability-ratio objective; value loss; entropy bonus; minibatch epochs over on-policy rollout batches.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

minds/deep_rl/torch_ppo_mind.py; test_phase3_deep_rl.py; outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv; Resource Island and other cross-world mind-comparison tables.

## Failure modes to audit

PPO label without clipped old-policy ratio; stale off-policy replay used as PPO; missing value baseline or advantage estimates; no entropy/value terms; only smoke tests without full-run comparison.

## Project code comparison

minds/deep_rl/torch_ppo_mind.py implements a structured-observation discrete PPO mind with Categorical actions, policy/value networks, rollout storage, GAE parameters, clipped surrogate objective, value loss, entropy coefficient, and minibatch epochs. That satisfies the thesis method obligation but does not reproduce the original continuous-control, Atari, sample-complexity, or wall-time benchmark suite.
